Optional .env file support via env_file parameter

NATSConfig and NATSClient construction with exact parameters
Per-episode ValueError handling for oversized bodies

completion_promises.criterion_text: guardkit/memory/harvest_publisher.py reads GUARDKIT_NATS_PASSWORD from the environment (optionally from an --env-file pointing at nats-infrastructure/.env); a missing/blank password raises an actionable error naming the variable and where to set it (does not connect with a blank pw).
completion_promises.evidence: Implemented build_nats_client() function that reads GUARDKIT_NATS_PASSWORD from environment or optional env_file. Raises ValueError with actionable message if password is missing or blank. Tests verify both missing and blank password cases raise with appropriate error messages.

completion_promises.criterion_text: Builds NATSConfig(url="nats://127.0.0.1:4222", user="guardkit", password=SecretStr(<pw>), name="guardkit-harvest") and NATSClient(cfg, source_id="guardkit-harvest").
completion_promises.evidence: build_nats_client() creates NATSConfig with exact parameters specified: url='nats://127.0.0.1:4222', user='guardkit', password wrapped in SecretStr, name='guardkit-harvest'. NATSClient is created with source_id='guardkit-harvest'. Tests verify all parameters are correct.

completion_promises.criterion_text: Publish lifecycle: await client.connect() → for each episode await client.publish_episode(ep) → await client.disconnect() (.disconnect(), not .close()).
completion_promises.evidence: publish_episodes() implements exact lifecycle: await client.connect(), then loops through episodes calling await client.publish_episode(ep), finally await client.disconnect(). Uses disconnect() not close(). Test verifies correct ordering with mock assertions.

completion_promises.criterion_text: A publish_episode ValueError (body > 900 KB) is caught per episode: that episode is skipped and recorded with an actionable message (path/episode_id + size + "chunk upstream"); the loop continues — one oversized doc never aborts the run.
completion_promises.evidence: ValueError from publish_episode is caught per episode in try/except block. Skipped episodes are counted in result.skipped_oversized and logged with episode_id, size, and 'chunk upstream' message. Loop continues to next episode. Tests verify oversized episode is skipped with actionable message and run is not aborted.

completion_promises.criterion_text: Idempotent / resumable: no client-side dedupe state; correctness relies on the deterministic episode_id → Nats-Msg-Id JetStream dedupe. Re-running publishes the same ids.
completion_promises.evidence: Implementation has no client-side deduplication state. All episodes are published on every run with their deterministic episode_ids. JetStream handles deduplication server-side via Nats-Msg-Id header (set by publish_episode). Test verifies re-running publishes the same episode_ids.

completion_promises.criterion_text: Does not hand-roll NATS publishing, subject construction, or the Nats-Msg-Id header — those are owned by publish_episode.
completion_promises.evidence: Implementation delegates all NATS operations to NATSClient.publish_episode(). No manual subject construction, no manual header setting, no direct NATS client calls. The publish_episode method handles all NATS protocol details.

completion_promises.criterion_text: Returns a publish summary: published, skipped_oversized, counts_per_type.
completion_promises.evidence: publish_episodes() returns PublishResult dataclass containing published (int), skipped_oversized (int), and counts_per_type (dict[str, int]). Result is populated during publish loop and verified by tests.

completion_promises.criterion_text: Unit tests use a fake/mock NATSClient (no live broker) asserting: connect → N × publish_episode → disconnect ordering; the >900 KB episode is skipped with the actionable error; the run never aborts on a single oversized item.
completion_promises.evidence: All tests use AsyncMock(spec=NATSClient) with no live broker connection. Tests verify: connect/publish/disconnect ordering, oversized episodes are skipped with actionable messages, and runs continue after oversized episodes. 14 tests pass covering all scenarios.
